analysis.title: GS MORNING: 1) CPI Preview, 2) G10 Spot Colour, 3) USDCNH Fixing Trend and 4) Equities Update
key_insights: GS US Economics (Mericle) expects October core CPI +0.16% m/m vs +0.2% consensus and headline +0.21% vs +0.3% consensus, with higher food and energy prices lifting headline. The forecast is consistent with a 0.23% rise in core PCE for October.

Component calls for October CPI: airfares unchanged m/m, medical services -0.1% (health insurance -2.5% as BLS updates its premium source data), and slower autos inflation (used cars -1.5%, new cars +0.1%, auto insurance -0.3%).
GS expects core CPI of about 0.1% m/m in both November and December, on slowing shelter, shrinking tariff pass-through and continued downward pressure from health insurance.

G10 FX spot desk (Brauten-Smith) says natural USD buying tied to hyperscaler Eurobond issuance looks finished. Yesterday there was no indiscriminate USD bid, and G10 FX began to acknowledge the prior week's energy moves.

Participation in G10 FX is light given performance strain on discretionary investors. The desk expects low volumes unless today's US CPI gives a decisive m/m reading. Tomorrow is a US holiday (stocks open, bonds closed, no USD settlement).
The FX desk is tilting its books toward a weaker USD versus JPY and GBP, after holding tactical USD length versus EUR last week.

The desk favours GBP longs over EUR because the UK does not include France. It holds mid-December 1.3700 GBPUSD calls with a cash overlay and expects GBPUSD to be high-beta on a USD sell-off because it has a smaller natural offer.

AUDNZD is -1.6% on the month, with November seasonality favouring lower. NZ elections trimmed the left tail on NZD, but the RBNZ held at end-October when +24bps was priced, and NZ employment data was weaker.

GS lists 'playing a French deterioration' as probably second on its 2027 trade list so far, behind short USDJPY/XXXJPY. Late September/early October price action showed appetite to press the French fiscal trade.

GS EM Strategy (Rastogi) believes the CNH appreciation trend remains intact after last week's FX reserve ratio hike. It favours adding to short USDCNH once the spot-fixing gap narrows back to 200-300 pips.
GS expects stronger-than-usual December exporter repatriation and a USDCNH grind lower toward 6.55-6.57 by end-January. The fixing is watched as a gauge of the authorities' intentions.

The USDCNH fix has deviated at most about 0.4% from its year-to-date trend line in either direction. The August episode peaked at 0.38%, and GS uses it to simulate how far the fix could diverge while staying consistent with the YTD pattern.

Privorotsky (GS equities flow) says Monday brought a strong recovery, with tech back on the front foot, Nvidia weakness contained and energy sharply lower. He calls the prior stretch one of the most aggressive net/gross de-risking episodes in the US prime book in a decade.

An in-line or softer CPI would challenge the roughly 80% priced probability of a December Fed hike, or shift risk to a March hike, which he says makes the setup considerably more constructive. Risks are a hot CPI and renewed Middle East escalation into the weekend. Vol tends to be autocorrelated after a violent rally.
The first neocloud to report after the midterms does so today. The question is whether contracted capacity earns attractive returns after financing costs, delays and depreciation, not demand.
The market is compartmentalising Nvidia's company-specific leadership headlines instead of selling the whole AI complex. Privorotsky says this is not the same as deteriorating AI demand.

The bipartisan data-center permitting bill cleared its first Senate procedural vote 73-25. It is not final passage and the House is likely the bigger obstacle. He expects data centers to be built with more conditions, not a nationwide moratorium. CEG rose 10% on stronger numbers, higher guidance and added generation agreements.

Positioning and sentiment remain shell-shocked while impulses, energy, rates and credit are supportive. A re-grossing trade would involve a steeper curve, a recovery in growth expectations and high beta/momentum regaining leadership. If CPI gives bonds a reason to rally, short covering could turn into a more sustainable re-grossing cycle.

Privorotsky sees the medium/long-term AI risk as compute oversupply or efficiency gains, not undersupply. He names aerospace, transports, select discretionary and high-quality unlevered AI as natural areas to chase into year-end if energy and inflation align.

vol_and_positioning: Privorotsky says the past stretch was one of the most aggressive net/gross de-risking episodes in the GS US prime book in a decade, and that positioning and sentiment remain shell-shocked and diminished.
After a violent rally off the lows, vol tends to be autocorrelated, so he advises local vigilance. The risks are a hot CPI and Middle East escalation into the weekend.
G10 FX participation is light, with discretionary investors under performance strain and low volumes expected absent a decisive CPI reading.
Hedge: GS FX owns mid-December GBPUSD 1.3700 calls with a cash overlay.
geopolitical: Middle East: Privorotsky describes a situation that is 'at least not escalating' and lists renewed escalation into the weekend as an obvious risk. Energy fell sharply.
US midterms: the market is said to have misread the election outcome on data-center policy. A bipartisan permitting bill cleared a first Senate procedural vote 73-25.
NZ elections: incumbents will form the base of a coalition with no dual mandate, trimming the left tail for NZD.
French fiscal risk: GS says late September/early October price action showed appetite to press a French deterioration trade.
